candidates.explanation: The 'items' property (a Set) is accessed and modified from multiple threads (the main thread in 'download' and potentially other threads via 'load') without any synchronization mechanism, which can lead to data races.
candidates.title: Thread Safety Issue

evidence.description: Subscription list is initialized but never updated or cleared

candidates.explanation: The 'subscriptions' property is an array of 'Subscription' objects that are never cleared or removed when a subscription is completed or cancelled, which can lead to a memory leak.
candidates.title: Potential Memory Leak

candidates.explanation: The 'hash(into:)' method only combines the 'url' property, while the '==' operator only checks the 'url' property. However, the 'Item' struct contains a 'data' property that is not included in the equality or hash calculations, which can lead to unexpected behavior if multiple different data payloads are associated with the same URL.
candidates.title: Inconsistent Hashable Implementation

evidence.description: Optional chaining on self inside async block

candidates.explanation: The use of [weak self] in the download completion handler is correct, but the subsequent optional chaining on 'self?.send(item)' and 'self?.items.insert(item)' means the operation will silently fail if 'Images' is deallocated before the network request completes.
candidates.title: Weak Self Reference in Closure
